purpose: Non-admission discovery of published Swiss radar hail storm-object predictors and crowdsourced label benchmark; no original source bytes, model admission, or insurer data.

entries.name: Swiss Storm-Object Radar Predictors and Crowdsourced Hail Labels v1
entries.provider: Martin Aregger / University of Bern / MeteoSwiss research / Zenodo
entries.spatial_scope: Switzerland and approximate 50 km buffer around the national border
entries.temporal_scope: Convective storms 2020-2024; deposited public v1 2026-01-02; companion 2026 peer-reviewed hail detection publication
entries.resolution_or_granularity: One ~3.7 GB ZIP 'radar_predictors.zip', publisher MD5 d461e6dd7a606a1cd1933da49f774d3a; object-based polarimetric C-band radar predictors with matched crowdsourced hail labels for tracked Thunderstorms Radar Tracking (TRT) cells; original internal row schema and counts unverified
entries.note: Original publisher Zenodo v1 declares CC BY 4.0; this is not a separate blanket permission for upstream raw MeteoSwiss radar observations or original crowdsourced reports. Paper 'Hail Detection and Sizing for Storm Objects: A Random Forest Framework Using Swiss C-Band Radar and Crowdsourced Reports' (online 2026-08-04): https://journals.ametsoc.org/view/journals/aies/5/3/AIES-D-26-0001.1.xml . Reproduction code: https://github.com/MartinAregger/HailForest_publication. Publisher file name and MD5 are recorded from Zenodo, but no ZIP bytes downloaded and no SHA-256 independently observed. Label occurrence, report completeness, temporal leakage and same-storm train/holdout grouping must be checked. This is a hazard observation/classification benchmark, not hailstone diameter ground truth for every cell, an insurer claims database, vulnerability curve or stochastic year catalogue.
